title: Read-only Claude delegations refuse `git check-attr`, a read-only command reviewers need to check .gitattributes effects
outcome: A read-only Claude delegation can run `git check-attr` (for example `git check-attr -a <path>`) to see the attributes, such as eol and text, that Git's clean/eol normalization applies to a reviewed file. Options that could write or run external programs stay refused, as for the other allowed subcommands.
acceptance: CLAUDE_READ_ONLY_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS (src/claude_read_only_refusal.rs) admits `check-attr`, with an option check equivalent to the other allowed subcommands; a regression test shows `git check-attr -a <path>` and `git check-attr --all -- <path>` admitted in a read-only Claude delegation, and an unchecked or writing option still refused.
The Codex and Kimi read-only policies are checked for the same gap, and either already admit `git check-attr` or are fixed the same way, with a test each.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
